transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO - OlivePeak), Lina Gomez (Infra Lead), Marcus Chen (SRE), Aisha Rahman (Product)

Auto-summary: Quick discovery focused on reserved GPUs (Dedicated), isolation needs for multi-tenant workloads, burst strategy (prewarm/hotpool), fallback to Redwood Hosted, and high-level pilot mechanics. Customer wants clarity on eviction behavior, VPC/KMS integration, and cost predictability.

Topics:
- Current infra and pain points
- Expected traffic and burst patterns
- Isolation and data residency / VPC needs
- Prewarm/hotpool and eviction/fallback strategy
- Pilot scope and decision criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, this is Jordan from Redwood, AE. we have Priya from our infra team as well. Can you hear us okay?
[00:05] Samir Patel: Yeah yep loud and clear, thanks. Good to meet you all.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi Samir, Lina, Marcus, thanks for the time. The goal for us is to understand your workload so we can map Dedicated or Private paths and where Hosted could be a fallback.
[00:22] Lina Gomez: Great. High level — OlivePeak runs mainly a low-latency scoring service for customer search suggestions and real-time enrichments. 80% of traffic is short requests but we get big spikes when a new dataset rolls out or during end-of-day batch re-ranking. Spikes can be 10x baseline for 5-10 minutes.
[00:40] Marcus Chen: Also we have multi-tenant models — some tenants are regulated so we'd need stronger tenant isolation, possibly dedicated nodes per tenant group.
[00:50] Priya Kapoor: Okay interesting. When you say dedicated nodes per tenant group, do you mean physical tenancy or logically isolated on the same GPU?
[00:58] Marcus Chen: Prefer physical isolation if possible for a subset of customers — basically reserved GPU pools for compliance customers. For others we can share with strict QoS.
[01:08] Jordan Meyers: Makes sense. We call that Dedicated with tenancy fences — you can reserve a set of GPUs and assign tenancy rules, plus a warm pool for burst. One pattern is reserved capacity + hotpool for spiky workloads.
[01:20] Samir Patel: A couple questions right away: 1) how do you handle eviction? 2) if we go Dedicated and there's a huge spike beyond reserved, can we fall back to Redwood Hosted automatically and what are the data controls there?
[01:31] Priya Kapoor: Great questions. Eviction is controlled by your policy — you can set preemption tolerance and tenant priority. For fallback, we support smart routing: if your Dedicated pool is saturated, requests can be routed to a Hosted model variant (if you accept the tradeoff) or queued with graceful degradation. We can surface per-route rules in the Console.
[01:50] Lina Gomez: When you say Hosted, does that mean data leaves our VPC? We need to know about network and encryption.
[01:58] Priya Kapoor: If you choose automatic fallback to Hosted, the request payload would traverse Redwood's hosted environment. For regulated tenants we usually recommend Private or Dedicated-only with strict peering; or we can architect a hybrid where only non-sensitive routes fall back. We support TLS in transit, and KMS integrations for keys — but you should plan for data residency and audit logs.
[02:20] Marcus Chen: How mature is KMS/HSM support? We have enterprise KMS policies and need customer-managed keys for models and logs.
[02:27] Jordan Meyers: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers and offer HSM-backed flows for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can provide KMS integration and ensure audit logs are shipped to your SIEM, but details depend on whether you choose our Reserved Dedicated (cloud-hosted but isolated) or Private (VPC + control plane in your environment).
[02:45] Aisha Rahman: From product side, our decision criteria are cost, latency tail, and compliance. If Dedicated reduces variability and predictable cost, that's a big plus. We also want a clear escalation path if things go sideways.
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: Totally. For cost predictability we advise reserved commitments with a burst allowance. You can buy X reserved GPUs and configure burst credits to allow ephemeral scale. We also have tooling (Optimize) to recommend quantization and batching to reduce tokens per inference.
[03:15] Samir Patel: On the burst behavior — you mentioned prewarm and hotpool. Can you explain how long prewarmed KV-cache remains valid and how that affects latency on sudden spikes?
[03:26] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Prewarming keeps model weights loaded and some KV cache warmed for typical prefixes; the hotpool nodes maintain a warmed environment for a configurable TTL. In practice we've seen 90% reduction in cold-start latency when TTL is set to 15-30 minutes for similar workloads. But long TTL consumes reserved capacity, so it's a tradeoff.
[03:43] Marcus Chen: Is there an API to control eviction and TTL programmatically?
[03:47] Priya Kapoor: Yes there is. Console exposes defaults and API exposes per-model/per-route overrides. You can also tie policies to token budgets and per-tenant caps.
[03:56] Jordan Meyers: Quick qualification — what is your expected QPS and model family? That will affect GPU type and count.
[04:03] Samir Patel: Baseline is ~150 QPS across all tenants. Peak can hit 1.5k QPS briefly during dataset publishes. Model family is a mixture — staff are testing both Llama-derivative open models and some parameter-reduced transformer variants. Sequence length is typically under 256 tokens.
[04:20] Priya Kapoor: Great — that gives us room to recommend node sizing. For 1.5k peak with low seq length we may suggest dedicated a mix of A100/RTX8000 equivalent or multi-GPU partitions, depending on whether you want more concurrency vs larger batch throughput.
[04:33] Lina Gomez: Are there recommended isolation topologies? We're debating per-tenant GPU pools vs cgroup-level QoS and sched optimizations.
[04:40] Priya Kapoor: For regulated tenants we recommend physical separation (node-level), for others we recommend tenant sharding with strict request quotas and hotpool affinity. We have eviction guards so a misbehaving tenant doesn't take down the whole reserved pool.
[04:54] Samir Patel: Another operational question: what's the expected ramp time to provision Dedicated nodes? We need to know lead time for Reserved capacity.
[05:02] Jordan Meyers: For cloud-hosted Dedicated it's usually a 2-6 week lead time depending on GPU type and region. Private/on-prem packaging has a longer procurement path. For near-term pilots we can do a small reserved set and use Hosted overflow.
[05:14] Marcus Chen: Cost — can you share an example cost breakdown? We want a clear comparison: hosted per-token vs dedicated amortized per-GPU + utilization assumptions.
[05:23] Jordan Meyers: We'll send a spreadsheet. High level: dedicated is capitalized cost amortized across reserved months; utilization is the leverage. If you maintain 60-80% utilization during business hours, dedicated often wins. If usage is highly spiky and low sustained, hosted can be cheaper.
[05:38] Aisha Rahman: On pilot scope — we'd want a 2-week perf run with realistic traffic and an SLO for 99th percentile latency. Also a security review before any real-data runs.
[05:48] Priya Kapoor: That's standard. Pilot would include a model baseline run, KV-cache warm cycles, prewarm config tuning, and a throughput spike test to validate fallback routing. We'll provide test harness scripts.
[05:59] Samir Patel: On fallback routing: if overflow moves to Hosted, how do you monitor and alert? We need originate-to-sink tracing so we can tell which requests hit hosted vs dedicated.
[06:08] Priya Kapoor: Console traces requests and tags them with route origin; we can add an extra request header or logging sink for your SIEM. You can set alerts on fallback percentage.
[06:16] Lina Gomez: About logs and audit — retention policies, do you allow us to ship raw request logs to our S3 or SIEM?
[06:22] Jordan Meyers: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can ship audit logs to your storage endpoints with configurable retention. For Hosted we keep logs per policy but can stream to your sinks as part of an enterprise package.
[06:35] Samir Patel: What about model versions and rollouts? If we push a new model and latency regresses, what's the rollback pattern?
[06:41] Priya Kapoor: We support canary rollouts by percentage and automatic fallback if quality or latency drops. Optimize can also monitor prompt set regressions. Rollbacks can be automated based on evals you define.
[06:52] Marcus Chen: A technical deep question — for very bursty workloads, is it better to overprovision reserved GPUs or rely on hotpools+fallback? We want to avoid paying for constant overprovisioning.
[07:02] Priya Kapoor: It depends on your acceptable failure modes. Hotpools reduce cost by only being warm for short windows; fallback ensures availability but with potential cost/latency implications. The middle ground is a small reserved baseline sized for 95th percentile plus hotpool and a small burst credit. We can model cost across scenarios.
[07:18] Samir Patel: Okay, good. On compliance — SOC 2 is a must for us. Do you have that? Any ISO certs?
[07:24] Jordan Meyers: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We also have ISO 27001 in our roadmap; we'll share the attestation docs and the network diagram. For Private deployments we can satisfy stricter controls.
[07:36] Aisha Rahman: Do you have examples of customers that shifted from Hosted to Dedicated and what their cost delta looked like?
[07:42] Jordan Meyers: Yes we can anonymize a few case studies. Typically customers with steady throughput and high tail sensitivity saw 20-40% unit-cost reductions after switching to Dedicated with right quantization and batching. We'll include an example in the follow-up.
[07:56] Lina Gomez: Can we get a small POC — say 2 reserved GPUs for two weeks to validate latency and fallback? If we can prove it, procurement will work on a larger commitment.
[08:06] Jordan Meyers: Absolutely. A two-week pilot on 2 GPUs with burst to Hosted for overflow is doable. We'd run load tests, warm cycles, and validate telemetry.
[08:14] Marcus Chen: Network details — VPC peering vs private link? We prefer private link for tighter control. Any limitations?
[08:20] Priya Kapoor: We support both peering and PrivateLink/Direct Connect depending on region. For Private deployments we do control-plane connectivity adjustments. We'll send network diagrams and the list of allowed endpoints.
[08:32] Samir Patel: SLA — what's your uptime and latency SLA for Dedicated?
[08:36] Jordan Meyers: For Dedicated we provide SLA commitments on uptime and best-effort latency SLOs; exact numbers depend on contract tier. Premium SLAs include higher availability guarantees and faster incident response.
[08:48] Aisha Rahman: Any gotchas we should watch for during pilot?
[08:51] Priya Kapoor: Watch for cache warming patterns — synthetic traffic often doesn't warm caches like production traffic. Also, model tokenization differences can impact latency; we'll advise using a representative prompt set.
[09:04] Samir Patel: Ok that's helpful. Timeline wise we aim to decide on a path within the next three weeks. Procurement is sensitive to lead times and committed spend.
[09:12] Jordan Meyers: Understood. We'll get the pricing and pilot plan to you by next Monday. Could we schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of 2025-10-27?
[09:20] Samir Patel: That works tentatively. I'll confirm after internal check.
[09:24] Jordan Meyers: Great. Any final questions?
[09:28] Marcus Chen: One small note — can Redwood provide a sample eviction policy for review so we can map to our oncall runbooks?
[09:34] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have templates for eviction/preemption that we can share.
[09:38] Aisha Rahman: We'll want to review the contract wording around data flows for fallback to Hosted — particularly deletion and retention clauses.
[09:45] Jordan Meyers: We'll flag legal and include those items.
[09:48] Samir Patel: Thanks all. Good call.

Recap/Decisions:
- Pilot agreed: 2 reserved GPUs, 2-week perf run, fallback to Hosted enabled for non-sensitive routes.
- Redwood to share pricing, SOC2 & network diagrams, eviction policy templates, and prewarm/hotpool recommendations.
- OlivePeak to share traffic profiles, decision timeline, and compliance constraints.

Close: Jordan: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with a single email with artifacts and next steps.

[End of transcript]
